title: Determining the Dues Settlement Figure on a Circle Membership
content:
## 1. Where the figure comes from

The figure a member must pay to bring a Circle membership back into good standing is worked out from the
membership ledger itself and never from the running dues figure shown on the membership record, which is
refreshed only when the nightly collection run reaches it.

## 2. The entries counted

The entries counted are the dues charges and the dues payments booked in the twelve months ending on the
handling day.

## 3. The two sides

The dues side is the total of the annual dues charges and the proration charges among the entries counted,
and the payments side is the total of the dues payments among them. The payments side is taken off the dues
side once, on the whole of it, before anything further is added or set against it.

## 4. Combining the parts

The parts are combined in one sum, in this order: the dues side less the payments side, plus the fee for
putting the standing right, less the store credit set against the amount, plus what is owed on the plan,
plus what is owed on the return and less what is owed to the member on it. That sum is rounded to the
nearest cent only at the end, no intermediate being rounded, and the figure never falls below nothing.

## 5. Where the money goes and when it may be taken

The money received is applied to the oldest unpaid billing period first, and any remainder to the next.
Dues are billed, and payments applied, only while the membership record stands as an application received,
active or in grace.

## 6. The figure worked through on hypothetical entries

Take a membership on Circle Plus Annual whose counted entries carry one annual dues charge of 49.99 and one
proration charge of 14.00, against dues payments of 20.00, and take the fee for putting the standing right,
the store credit set against the amount, what is owed on the plan and what is owed on the return all at
nothing for this illustration. The dues side is 63.99, the payments side is 20.00, and taking the payments
side off the whole of the dues side leaves 43.99. Nothing further is added or set against it, so the figure
rounded at the end is 43.99, and the money is applied first to the oldest of the unpaid periods among those
entries.
